answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can tie each identity to a staked bond that only unlocks after peers attest real work. Picture a wharf where every ship pays a docking fee: a new vertex in the trust graph starts at the jetty with a small stake, and only earns a bigger berth once other agents vouch for its deliveries. Fake accounts then cost real money to spin up, and one bad actor loses its bond across all its identities at once.
